record.context_brief: vanishing singular part for relaxed harmonic-map minimizers
record.original_question: Let u be a minimizer of the relaxed energy R in the B^3-to-S^2 harmonic-map problem. The source represents R(u) as integral_Omega |grad u|^2 + S(u), where S(u) measures topological singularities through the distributional Jacobian J u. Must S(u)=0, equivalently J u=0, for such a minimizer? Equivalently, can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in H^1 by maps in H^1_g(Omega; S^2) that are continuous on the closed ball?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = B^3 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be the open unit ball, and let $g : \partial\Omega \to S^2$ be a fixed smooth boundary datum. Consider the Sobolev space
$$H^1_g(\Omega; S^2) = \{ u \in H^1(\Omega; \mathbb{R}^3) : |u|=1 \text{ a.e. in } \Omega,\ u|_{\partial\Omega}=g\}.$$
For $u \in H^1_g(\Omega; S^2)$ define the distributional Jacobian
$$J u = \tfrac{1}{2} \, d\!\left(u^1\, du^2 \wedge du^3 + u^2\, du^3\wedge du^1 + u^3\, du^1\wedge du^2\right),$$
viewed as a distribution; equivalently, writing $D(u) = (u\cdot u_{x_2}\wedge u_{x_3},\ u\cdot u_{x_3}\wedge u_{x_1},\ u\cdot u_{x_1}\wedge u_{x_2})$, one has $\operatorname{div} D(u) = 4\pi \sum_i d_i\, \delta_{a_i}$ for maps with isolated point singularities of degrees $d_i$ at $a_i$. Define the singular ("length of minimal connection") functional
$$L(u) = \sup\Big\{ \int_\Omega D(u)\cdot \nabla\zeta\,dx : \zeta\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega),\ |\nabla\zeta|\le 1,\ \zeta|_{\partial\Omega}\text{ chosen compatibly with }g\Big\},$$
and put $S(u) = 4\pi L(u)$, so $S(u)=0$ if and only if $J u = 0$ (modulo the contribution of the boundary datum $g$). The relaxed Dirichlet energy is
$$R(u) = \int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2\,dx + S(u),$$
which coincides with the sequentially weak $H^1$-lower semicontinuous envelope of the Dirichlet energy restricted to the maps in $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$.

Question: If $u \in H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ is a minimizer of $R$ on $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$, must $S(u) = 0$, equivalently $J u = 0$? Equivalently, can every such minimizer be approximated strongly in $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3)$ by maps in $H^1_g(\Omega;S^2)$ that are continuous on $\overline\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as an open problem in Brezis's collection of favorite open problems, and current literature on minimizers of the relaxed energy for harmonic maps from $B^3$ to $S^2$ (e.g., works of Bethuel–Brezis–Coron and follow-up partial regularity results) discusses partial regularity of such minimizers but does not establish vanishing of the singular part $S(u)$. No publication appears to resolve the question of whether $S(u)=0$ for every minimizer.

status_evidence.title: On the minimizers of the relaxed energy functional of mappings from higher dimensional balls into S^2
status_evidence.snippet: Partial regularity results for minimizers of the relaxed energy with singularity current S_u.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work proves only partial regularity properties of relaxed-energy minimizers, not vanishing of the singular part.
